summary: The bill amends the Uniform Code of Military Justice to criminalize service members knowingly broadcasting or distributing authentic or digitally forged intimate images of identifiable people without consent when it causes or intends harm, with separate rules for minors and listed exceptions.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, budgets, or expenditures of any kind. It solely modifies the Uniform Code of Military Justice.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or delivery systems.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill has no immigration, border, or visa-related content.
No provisions concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill amends the UCMJ (a military justice statute), it does not address defense budgets, troop levels, procurement, or spending levels.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions are present.
The bill does not modify any welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs.
No education funding, school policy, or curriculum provisions exist.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions.

The bill expands the scope of punishable conduct under Article 117a of the UCMJ by adding digital forgeries, clarifying consent standards, and broadening harm definitions. This constitutes an increase in criminal prohibitions and potential penalties within the military justice system, aligning with the 'tougher sentencing and policing' direction.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are included.
The bill has no fiscal, deficit, or debt-related provisions.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign assistance or international aid provisions.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign-related content.

The bill regulates the broadcast and distribution of intimate images and AI-generated digital forgeries via communication services, imposing new consent and harm-based restrictions on online publication within the military context. This increases oversight of technology platforms and strengthens privacy protections against nonconsensual imagery.
No labor, union, or employment-law provisions.
No religious exemptions, civil-rights balancing, or anti-discrimination measures are present.
